notes:
Summary: Stratagem is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for latency-sensitive fintech workloads (real-time pricing + support chatbot). Primary ask: predictable throughput and an explicit latency SLO in contract, plus EU-only residency and KMS separation.

Workload / SLO targets (customer-provided):
- Primary path: real-time pricing API (256-token average) -> p95 latency target < 120ms; p99 < 250ms under steady state
- Secondary: support-agent chat (streaming) -> target end-to-end 300ms p95 for short messages
- Throughput planning: baseline 120-180 reqs/sec, burst to 450 reqs/sec during market open windows
- Embeddings batch jobs nightly (non-latency sensitive) to use burst capacity / scheduled windows.

Reserved capacity ask / sizing:
- Customer prefers reserved pool to guarantee throughput. Preliminary sizing request: equivalent to 4x A100-80GB or 2x H100 per region with autoscale headroom for bursts. Wants concrete throughput-per-GPU metrics and guidance for buffer planning.
- Wants deterministic cold-start behavior and KV cache warm-up expectations documented.

Commercial / SLA negotiation points (procurement and legal):
- DPA / MSA redlines: Stratagem insists on stricter limits around permitted data processing, deletion timelines, and audit rights. Their legal proposes removal of Redwood's standard data usage clause.
- Liability & Indemnity: they requested higher liability cap for regulated transactions (legal flagged need for separate carve-out).
- Insurance: procurement requires proof of cyber insurance with limits >= $5M; current Redwood COI is below their minimum.
- SLA: asking for latency-based credits (not just uptime). Example ask: if p95 latency exceeds agreed threshold over calendar month, service credits apply pro-rata. Redwood standard SLA covers availability only — gap.
- Compliance add-on: Stratagem wants Redwood to support an ISO audit and provide evidence packages; they request timeline and cost impact upfront. This add-on delays signing until audit scope agreed.

Operational notes / concerns:
- They will pin to a specific model family (open model preferred) and want model version pinning + automated fallback rules documented (what happens during capacity constraints).
- Request for explicit routing/region failover policy: EU primary, fallback to EU-dedicated spare region only; no cross-border failover without explicit approval.
- Cost sensitivity: willing to commit to a 12–24 month reserved contract if SLA and DPA terms acceptable; wants clear uplift for compliance add-ons.

Quote from procurement: "We can commit to reserved capacity if legal and security gaps are closed — especially DPA scope and insurance. SLA credits for latency are non-negotiable for trading side."

Open items / next actions:
- Legal: review Stratagem DPA redlines and provide counterproposal (owner: Redwood legal). Target 2026-03-16.
- Insurance: ops to obtain updated COI and options to meet $5M requirement (owner: Redwood ops).
- SE: provide throughput-per-GPU baseline report and recommended reserved sizing (deliverable: capacity model + runbook) by 2026-03-12 (owner: Liam Chen).
- Contract call w/ procurement + legal booked for 2026-03-18 to resolve SLA credit language and finalize pricing for compliance add-on.

CRM notes tone: fragments, high priority, procurement-driven. Purchasing authority: Head of Trading (signed term sheet level). Decision criteria: legal signoff + SLA latency credits + insurance.
